subject.title: fix(cli): reject --channel/--to for systemEvent cron jobs with a clear error

question: Should cron add and edit immediately fail when existing invocations supply chat-delivery flags that were previously accepted but ineffective for main system-event jobs?
rationale: The patch is technically coherent, but choosing a hard error instead of a warning or deprecation period changes observable CLI behavior for existing automation and cannot be settled by tests alone.

options.title: Approve consistent fail-fast validation
options.body: Reject the ineffective flags in both add and edit, document the behavior change, and require refreshed exact-head checks before merge.

options.title: Introduce a deprecation warning first
options.body: Continue accepting the flags temporarily while clearly warning that they have no effect, then convert the warning to an error in a later release.

options.title: Preserve current CLI acceptance
options.body: Leave enforcement to the gateway and avoid adding a new client-side failure, accepting less immediate feedback for users.

recommendation.title: Approve consistent fail-fast validation
recommendation.body: Reject the ineffective flags in both add and edit, document the behavior change, and require refreshed exact-head checks before merge.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent merged work on the cron edit command makes this the best available owner for the add/edit compatibility contract.
